Q2 clearability — doctor exits 6 only for a record that can still be cleared; every other is named inert without failing. Arm B (a drop command) is rejected for 0.1.0.
Read them on WCLI-82 rather than from memory; they bind, and a message asserting one is not the record.

THE SCRATCH-CLONE MEASUREMENT (rv331b new finding 1)
Recorded in full on WCLI-82. One throwaway repository per state:
  state                                              new form            old form
  1. no tags (the dry run), baseline HEAD            exit 0, []          exit 0, []
  2. only the child tag v0.1.0, baseline             exit 0, []          EXIT 1, "No tags can
     refs/tags/v0.1.0^{commit}^                                           describe '<sha>'"
  3. prior v* v0.0.9 on an ancestor, same baseline   exit 0, [v0.0.9]    exit 0, [v0.0.9]
  4. forced failure (not a repository), HEAD         exit 128            exit 1
State 2 is the release failing after its tag was pushed, and it is invisible before the tag because a dry run can only produce state 1. The shipped fix is `git tag --list 'v*' --merged "$baseline" --sort=-v:refname`, first line, with set -e failing the step on a non-zero exit.

Not a release blocker — re-running the failed job is the remedy if it fires on the cut.

POST-APPROVE SEQUENCE (after rv331-ward188c APPROVES, on the lead's word, in this order)
1. Merge #188 into dev. ONE bare command, alone, with the SHA typed literally from the lead's APPROVE relay:
     gh pr merge 188 --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit <approved head SHA>
   Never composed — no gh pr view in front of it, no pipe, no `;`, no cd prefix; a composed command falls through the allow rule to the classifier and is refused on consent (DEC-9). If it refuses with "Head branch was modified", do NOT retry without the pin and do NOT re-read and merge: report that the head moved since the approval.
   Then confirm the LOCAL branch fix/WCLI-82-release-review-fix-round is actually gone; --delete-branch can leave it after a squash, and `git branch -D` is a separate deliberate step, not optional tidying.
2. Realign: `git fetch origin` then `git merge --ff-only origin/dev`, each bare and separate. Never `git reset --hard` (permission dialog, and it cannot tell behind from diverged).
3. Promote dev to main: open a PR dev->main, let the required checks go green on that exact SHA, then land with `git push origin origin/dev:main` — the remote-tracking ref, never local dev. Never GitHub's merge button. GitHub auto-marks the PR MERGED and creates no merge commit. Re-measure the rulesets first if in doubt: main has no rules; dev requires Check, Docs and Tracker integrity.
4. Annotated tag v0.1.0 at main's TIP: `git tag -a v0.1.0` then push the tag. The workflow checks the tag is annotated (REST ref read, object.type == "tag"), names package.json's version, and equals origin/main's tip; a tag behind the tip fails the build.
5. The Release: the tag push builds ward-darwin-arm64 + .sha256 on the Linux ARM64 runner and publishes through scripts/publish-release.mjs (draft, upload, publish). THE TAG-PUSH PATH AND THE RELEASE JOB ARE UNPROVEN until this runs; the dry-run path is proven. Record the sha256 and cdhash from the release notes. The job token reading the git ref is evidence, not proof: the same GET already runs in this workflow's release job, and reading a ref needs only contents: read, but the tag run is its first real exercise.
6. Then opum-fleet AC3: the private marketplace pin of opum-ward at the tag (T25 private half; WCLI-82 AC3).
7. Then the operator-sitting packet, scheduled by opum-doc: install from the Release, keychain re-approval, re-approve profiles named clearable by ward status/doctor, the T26 packaged-binary run, and the T26 real send at https://httpbin.org/bearer with a synthetic secret (DEC-246 (a1) D2 A). If httpbin fails at the sitting: retry once, then postpone and report; do not substitute an endpoint.

RAILS, unchanged
No tag, no push to main, no Release, no ~/.local/bin, no ~/.ward, no real credential, until the lead says so in words. The tag is the session's own permission dialog answered by opum-doc as the operator's proxy. Remove no worktree. Never push to #188's branch while it is under review.

SKILLS TO REACH FOR
opum-workflow:opum-handoff (restore/write), opum-workflow:opum-sdlc (branch, PR, merge, promotion, cleanup), lore (docs: query -> read -> sync -> check), opum-tool-output (keep tool output small), quest instructions task-execution before tracker writes.

GOTCHAS THIS SESSION EARNED
- `git describe` dies whenever the baseline has no matching tag, so its failure has to be read as a result. On a tag push the baseline is the tag's own parent, which that tag can never describe. `git tag --list --merged` separates the cases by exit code instead of by stderr text.
- A blanket test assertion like not.toMatch(/git describe/) fails on the workflow COMMENT that explains why the command went. Ban the invocation (`git describe --`), not the phrase. Same trap twice: not.toContain("git cat-file -t") hit its own comment too.
- The agent profiles sit at their exact budgets. Adding ADR or runbook prose turns several red at once (agent-profile-capacity, then agent-profile-pin-capacity, both exit 6, both the Docs job). Raising max_tokens is forbidden. Narrowing means RE-HOMING: node scripts/check-lore-agent-sources.mjs fails with "N concepts are in no specialist profile" if you simply delete a source, so move the concept to a profile that can hold it, and free the space by swapping out a source two or more profiles declare. Check both gates after every edit.
- A profile declaration fixture must use headers as a record of name -> value; `headers: []` is refused by normalizeProfile and silently makes every case in a test inert for the wrong reason.
- Commit messages containing backticks cannot go through `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"`; the guard refuses the shape. Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. Same for anything with backticks in a double-quoted argument.
- `git push` joined to any other command is refused by the opum-workflow guard. Run it bare and alone.
- `gh pr checks` reports zero rows briefly after a push. Wait on a MINIMUM row count as well as the absence of pending.
- gh pr merge --delete-branch was seen to fast-forward the local default branch itself. Still verify, and still re-check the local branch is gone.
- The ward eval: a case is 1.0 only when all three runs pass both scored graders (criteria, no-value-echo); skill-fired is display-only. Re-measure a single case with --case before spending on a full suite.
- Two messages from the lead crossed this session's turns more than once. Check the state before doing work an instruction asks for: WCLI-87 was already filed when the instruction to file it arrived.
